entries.heading: Witness Circles
entries.text: An original Bitcoin protocol for membership by mutual witnessing. Two to sixteen Taproot keys authorize one exact transaction, and the record exists only when the loop closes.

entries.heading: Terminology
entries.text: Circle One confirmed Bitcoin transaction that satisfies every rule in section 6 of the specification. It is the whole protocol object; there is no separate registration. Marker The 42 byte scriptPubKey at output 0: OP_RE

entries.heading: Indexer semantics
entries.text: Confirmation A Circle becomes authoritative at one confirmation in the best chain. There is no maturity period, no second protocol state, and no probabilistic threshold in the protocol itself. A product may render six co

entries.heading: Fees and sizes for every participant count
entries.text: All values assume 64 byte SIGHASH_DEFAULT signatures. Explicit SIGHASH_ALL adds one witness byte per such input, which can add at most one virtual byte for every four such inputs. N Weight Virtual bytes Fee at 1 sat/vB F

entries.heading: Limitations
entries.text: No privacy. A Circle deliberately links every participating input, and every same-key continuation, in public forever. This is the feature and the risk. No identity. One person can hold sixteen keys. Nothing in the proto

entries.heading: Security considerations
entries.text: For participants Every input you contribute is permanently and publicly associated with every other input in the Circle, including any later Circle that continues one of those lineages. A signature commits to all inputs

entries.heading: Changing a rule
entries.text: The rules on this site are final for protocol version 0x01 . New behaviour requires a new version byte with its own specification, threat model, schemas, cross-language vectors, activation policy and independent review.
